analysis.title: FSA Fixed Income Daily Commentary - 17 November 2026
key_insights: US Treasuries rallied modestly on Monday, ending a three-session run of higher yields, as investors sought safety during a sharp equity selloff and a steep fall in oil. Gains were concentrated in the 3Y-5Y belly, and the 5s30s curve steepened by 3 basis points.

FSA still sees the backdrop favoring higher yields because of hawkish Fed commentary and persistent inflation pressure. Markets price about one full 25bp hike at the December 9 FOMC, with the tightening cycle peaking near 4.725% around September 2027, roughly 3.3 more 25bp hikes.

Cleveland Fed President Hammack, a 2026 voter, favors raising rates at a steadier, more gradual pace. She said recent increases in market rates reflect resilient growth and expectations of further tightening, so financial conditions could tighten before the Fed changes its policy rate.

Fed Chair Warsh said the Fed has convened a task force on AI. Productivity has improved but shows no clear evidence of a durable upgrade to trend growth. Scenarios include AI investment failing to earn expected returns and AI displacing workers, which would raise unemployment.

The US Commerce Department issued interim rules restricting remote access to advanced US AI chips and servers. Singapore and Brazil face added export-licensing requirements, alongside Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand, because the US sees a higher-than-normal risk of diversion to China.

Global rate and FX moves: UK 10Y gilt yield rose 3bp to 5.365% and 2Y gilts topped 5%, the highest since October 2023. JGB 10Y rose 5.8bp to 2.899%. The dollar hit a 19-month high and gold a one-year low.

Weak October China data: retail sales +0.4% y/y, industrial output +4.8% y/y and fixed-asset investment -8.1% YTD, all worse than expected. New-home prices fell 0.15% m/m, resale prices fell 0.24% m/m and property investment is down nearly 22% YTD.
US Empire State Manufacturing Index fell to 7.8 in November from 25.5, far below the 18 consensus. Canada's October CPI came in below consensus at +0.2% m/m and 3.1% y/y, with core measures near 2%.

FSA upgraded XP (Brazil) from MP to OP on 3Q26 results it called credit positive: net revenue up 9% y/y, net cash of BRL12.3 billion, BIS ratio 20.3% and CET1 17.2%. Adjusted EPS of BRL2.69 was 3.9% below consensus.

Baidu (UP) reported 3Q26 results FSA called credit negative: revenue -1% y/y, Online Marketing Services -22% y/y, AI Cloud Infra +94% y/y, free cash flow of negative RMB4.57 billion, short-term loans up to RMB23.2 billion and net cash down to RMB129 billion from RMB150 billion at FY25.

Volvo Cars (UP) was cut by Moody's to Ba2 from Ba1 with a negative outlook. Free cash flow is expected to stay negative through 2027, net debt is SEK 15.6 billion and leverage is expected to peak above 5x in 2026.
Fitch upgraded BCP to A- from BBB+ and Devon Energy to A- from BBB+ on November 16. FSA stays MP on both. It called the BCP upgrade largely priced in and was not surprised by the Devon upgrade.

Tyson Foods (MP) beat on 4QFY26 sales and adjusted EPS but guided FY27 sales down 3.5% to 5.5%, below the consensus of a 1% fall, and free cash flow down to USD0.8-1.3 billion. FSA rated the results credit neutral.

Telus (UP) received an unsolicited non-binding proposal from Quebecor at about CAD19.45 per share, roughly a 60% premium by Quebecor's figure. Pro forma net leverage would be about 4.1x 2027E against Telus's 3.6x, and FSA views it as credit neutral.

Commerzbank (MP): the US Fed approved UniCredit's exchange offer and EU clearance was unconditional, with the final approval expected by November 30. UniCredit holds 37.81% of voting rights and expects control on settlement.

Debt calls and buybacks: Bombardier will redeem all USD750 million of its 8.750% 2030 notes on December 1 at 104.375, funded from cash. Nexa will redeem its USD111.0 million 6.500% 2028 notes on December 18, removing the series where an S&P downgrade alone triggers a 101% put.
Top picks added in the last 4 weeks: Sumitomo Life 5.308% EUR subordinated (YTM 5.80%), HSBC 7.625% USD perpetual (YTM 7.75%) and ING 7.750% USD perpetual (YTM 7.90%).

Other issuer updates rated MP or OP: Hapoalim (credit neutral, CET1 down to 11.62%), Kyobo Life (investment losses, in-force CSM above KRW7 trillion), J&J (USD2.2 billion Ollin Biosciences deal), Pegasus (buyback up to TRY3.00 billion), Ecopetrol and Davivienda (Brava and Scotiabank integration), Legal & General (Solvency II 213%) and Rumo (EBITDA -4%).

earnings_insights: Tyson Foods 4QFY26 reported 11/16: sales $14.6 billion (+5.2% y/y over 14 weeks vs 13) against consensus est $14.1 billion. Adjusted EPS $0.61 against consensus est $0.53. Adjusted operating income fell 41% to $361 million. FY27 guide: sales down 3.5% to 5.5% vs consensus est of a 1% fall.

Baidu 3Q26 reported 11/16: revenue RMB30.8 billion (-1% y/y), in line with consensus est RMB30.8 billion. Baidu General Business non-GAAP operating income RMB1.69 billion missed consensus est RMB1.8 billion. GAAP net income RMB1.40 billion.
XP 3Q26 reported 11/16: net revenue BRL5,139 million (+9% y/y), 0.8% above consensus est BRL5.10 billion. Adjusted diluted EPS BRL2.69 was 3.9% below consensus est BRL2.80.
Ecopetrol 3Q26 reported 11/12: EBITDA COP15,871 billion, about USD4,970.6 million, 8.7% above consensus est USD4,571.1 million. Net income attributable up 85.6%.
Legal & General 3Q26: Solvency II coverage 213% vs consensus est 212%. Asset Management Q3 net outflows of GBP3 billion were better than consensus est GBP4.5 billion.
Devon Energy 3Q26: production 1,668,000 Boe/d, adjusted free cash flow $2.0 billion. Repurchases expected above $1 billion in 4Q26 from $414 million in 3Q26.
Bank Hapoalim 3Q26 reported 11/16: net profit NIS2.36bn (flat vs NIS2.38bn in 3Q25 excluding a one-off, down from NIS2.76bn reported). ROE 14.0% vs 17.6%.
Kyobo Life 9M26: consolidated net profit to owners fell 19.9% y/y to KRW708 billion. 3Q26 consolidated net profit was KRW3.4 billion vs KRW302 billion in 3Q25.
Cosan 3Q26 reported 11/13: consolidated EBITDA BRL4.20 billion vs BRL2.71 billion a year earlier. Net income to controlling shareholders BRL190 million vs a loss of BRL1.19 billion.
Rumo 3Q26: adjusted EBITDA fell 4% to BRL2.2 billion on 3.5% revenue growth. Net leverage 2.2x.
Davivienda 3Q26: consolidated net profit fell 14.3% q/q to COP567bn, 9M26 earnings COP1.51tn, adjusted ROAE 11.5% vs 13.8%.

San Miguel Global Power 9M26 (SEC 17-Q): revenue PHP149.1 billion (+25% y/y), operating income PHP53.4 billion (+53%), net income PHP42.6 billion (+1%, versus PHP20.5 billion in 9M25 excluding a one-time gain).

risk_factors: Persistent inflation and hawkish Fed commentary could keep Treasury yields rising, tightening financial conditions before any policy move.
Heavy AI investment may fail to generate expected returns, which Warsh said could weigh on equities, spending and activity.
AI displacing rather than complementing workers could raise unemployment.
China's property downturn and developer credit stress, including repayment difficulties at Zhuhai Huafa Group, remain a drag on recovery.
A deterioration in US-Canada trade talks could push Canada toward closer ties with Chinese automakers.
Tighter US export controls on AI chips widen compliance and diversion-risk requirements across several Asian and Latin American jurisdictions.
Raizen's restructuring may significantly dilute Cosan and end joint control.
Boliden's closing of the Nexa stake purchase and Fitch's decision on Nexa remain open.
geopolitical: US Commerce Department interim rules restrict remote access to advanced US AI chips and servers, adding export-licensing requirements for Singapore and Brazil alongside Indonesia, Malaysia and Thailand.
President Trump said he has no plans to remove Commerce Secretary Lutnick despite scrutiny over whether the department has done enough to stop China obtaining advanced US technology.
Canadian PM Carney said Canada could expand commercial ties with Chinese automakers if trade talks with the US deteriorate.
Gulf bourses recovered early losses after Iranian aerial attacks on Bahrain (Reuters Arabic service, 16 Nov).
Sweden's centre-left parties are still arguing over how to share power two months after the election.
